title: Green Shito
author: Naa Adjei
desc: Green scotch bonnets, spring onion and garlic cooked five minutes to dry out, then fried ten in oil until the oil sets on top.
longDesc: The green counterpart to black shito, and much quicker: a brown onion, green scotch bonnets, half an inch of ginger, four or five garlic cloves and two spring onion stalks are blended, cooked on low to medium five minutes to dry out the extra liquid, then three quarters of a cup of vegetable oil goes in and it fries on medium ten minutes, or until the oil sets on top. Half a tablespoon of all-purpose seasoning finishes it. Her note on colour is the useful one: the longer the sauce cooks, the more it changes from bright green to darker green.
ingredients: 3 green scotch bonnet peppers — the method says 2, see the note
Garlic, a handful of cloves (4 or 5)
steps: Blend the onion, green scotch bonnets, ginger, garlic and spring onion stalks.
Cook on low to medium 5 minutes, to dry out the extra liquid.
Fry on medium 10 minutes, or until the oil sets on top.
Season with the all-purpose seasoning and salt.
chefTips: Dry it out for five minutes BEFORE the oil goes in. Oil into a wet purée will spit and the sauce will never set properly.
Until the oil sets on top is the cue, at about ten minutes. Same principle as black shito, much faster.
Her colour note is worth knowing: the longer it cooks, the more the colour goes from bright green to darker green. Stop early if you want it vivid.
Green scotch bonnets, not red. The green fruit is grassier and less sweet, and the colour is the point of the sauce.
Note the misprint: the ingredient list says three scotch bonnets, the method says two. Start at two and add the third if you want it hotter.
Ginger, garlic and spring onion all carry NO quantities in the ingredient list — the figures above come from the method, where they are stated.
A fresher, sharper condiment than black shito, and it does not keep nearly as long. Make it in small batches.
commonMistakes: Adding the oil to the wet blend.
Over-cooking, which turns the green dull.
Taking three peppers as settled when the method says two.
Making a large batch — it does not keep like black shito.
sources: Adapted from 'Ghanaian Green Pepper Sauce (Kpakoshito)', soulfulkitchenco.com. BYLINE FLAG: the byline and the site owner are both the SITE'S OWN NAME, with no person identified. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS). Page-level yield of '10 servings' appeared on one fetch only (SINGLE-PASS).

Ingredient list exactly as printed: 1 medium brown onion; 3 green scotch bonnet peppers; Ginger; Garlic; Spring onion stalks; All-purpose seasoning; Salt; ¾ cup vegetable oil. One fetch omitted the oil line from the list but gave it in the method. NOTE that ginger, garlic and spring onions carry NO QUANTITIES in the list.

Method as printed, which is where the missing quantities appear: blend '1 medium brown onion, 2 green scotch bonnet peppers, ½ inch of ginger, a handful of garlic cloves (4/5), and 2 spring onion stalks'; cook 'on low to medium temperature for 5 minutes to dry extra liquids'; add '¾ cup of vegetable oil' and fry 'on medium temperature for 10 minutes or until the oil sets on top'; season with '½ tbsp. of all-purpose seasoning'.

MISPRINT, flagged and NOT corrected: the ingredient list says 3 GREEN SCOTCH BONNETS while the method says 2. The two do not reconcile. Both are recorded; the ingredient list above prints three with a pointer to the discrepancy, and the tips advise starting at two.
THE DONENESS CUE, as printed: 'until the oil sets on top'. That is the same endpoint as black shito in a different form of words.
THE COLOUR NOTE, verbatim: 'The longer the sauce cooks, the more the color changes from bright green to darker green.' Useful, because it tells you the cue and the colour pull in opposite directions.

A GAP, named: NO OTHER ACCEPTABLE SOURCE for a Ga-specific green shito was found. The only other appearance of green kpakpo shito in the documented record is as an ingredient inside black shito — 75 g of them in the Splendid Table recipe at GHA051 — rather than as a sauce in its own right. So this is the sole documented green shito, which is why it is published despite a site-name byline and an internal misprint.
ON KPAKPO SHITO: the small round Ghanaian chilli. 'Kpakoshito' as the sauce name on this page is a variant spelling of the same word.
storage: 2 weeks refrigerated under its oil. Shorter-keeping than black shito.
reheating: Not needed. Served cold or at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Green chillies are very high in vitamin C.
Garlic, ginger and spring onion all carry documented antimicrobial compounds.
Vegan, unlike black shito, which depends on dried seafood.
Used by the spoonful, so the oil per serving is small.
culturalNote: Green shito is the fresher, sharper cousin of the black paste, and it is what you want beside grilled fish rather than beside kenkey. That only one documented recipe for it exists, against three for black shito, suggests it is more often made by eye than written down.
